key_insight: An algebraic multiscale coarse space built from interface-based reduced boundary condition problems can make two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners robust to strong coefficient heterogeneity while staying fully matrix-based.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical, scalable preconditioning strategy for large heterogeneous elliptic and elasticity problems, especially when geometric multiscale information is unavailable.
method: Construct coarse basis functions by solving algebraic reduced boundary condition problems on interface slabs.
Use energy-minimizing extensions so coefficient variations along interfaces are captured in the coarse space.
Embed the approach in an energy-minimizing framework to extend it from scalar diffusion to linear elasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method stays contrast-robust when high-coefficient inclusions sit on coarse nodes, matches GDSW iteration counts in 3D log-normal diffusion, and uses a coarse problem about ten times smaller.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the interface/slab construction captures the relevant heterogeneity, and elasticity requires careful handling of rigid body modes.
paper_title: An algebraic multiscale framework for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners
